## Perspective Audit Summary

**Component/artifact reviewed:** TabPanel component (`src/components/TabPanel.jsx` + `src/components/TabPanel.css`)  
**Perspectives escalated for deep review:** Keyboard Motor (HIGH), Screen Reader Semantic (HIGH)  
**Perspectives at LOW (not reviewed):** Magnification & Reflow, Environmental Contrast, Vestibular & Motion Sensitivity, Auditory Access, Cognitive & Neurodivergent

---

### Findings by Severity

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| CRITICAL | 0 |
| MAJOR | 4 |
| MINOR | 2 |
| ENHANCEMENT | 1 |

---

### Perspectives That Passed

None — both escalated perspectives have findings.

---

### Findings by ARRM Role

#### Front-End Dev

- **Missing ARIA roles and attributes for tablist pattern** — Screen Reader Semantic — MAJOR — WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value  
  - Evidence: `src/components/TabPanel.jsx` lines 20–35 — `<button>` elements lack `role="tab"`, parent `.tab-bar` lacks `role="tablist"`, panels lack `role="tabpanel"` and `aria-labelledby`/`aria-controls`. No WAI-ARIA APG tab pattern implemented.  
  - Fix: Add `role="tablist"` to container, `role="tab"` + `aria-selected`, `tabindex="-1"/"0"` on buttons, `role="tabpanel"` with `aria-labelledby` referencing each tab button ID.

- **No keyboard arrow-key navigation between tabs** — Keyboard Motor — MAJOR — WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard  
  - Evidence: `src/components/TabPanel.jsx` lines 16–35 — Only native `<button>` click handlers exist; no keydown listener for ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/Home/End to move focus/select adjacent tabs per WAI-ARIA APG tab pattern.  
  - Fix: Implement `onKeyDown` handler on each tab button supporting Left/Right arrows (move focus + activate), Home/End (first/last tab).

- **Panels hidden via inline style only — no ARIA state management** — Screen Reader Semantic — MAJOR — WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value  
  - Evidence: `src/components/TabPanel.jsx` lines 37–43 — Panels use `style={{ display: activeTab === tab.id ? 'block' : 'none' }}`. No `aria-hidden`, no focus management on panel switch, no programmatic association between tabs and panels. Screen readers may announce hidden content or fail to associate controls with their panels.  
  - Fix: Use `aria-hidden={activeTab !== tab.id}` on inactive panels; ensure active panel receives logical focus or is announced via live region if dynamic.

- **No visible focus indicator for mouse users who Tab into component** — Keyboard Motor — MINOR — WCAG 2.4.7 Focus Visible  
  - Evidence: `src/components/TabPanel.css` lines 38–41 — `:focus-visible` only triggers after keyboard interaction; if a user tabs directly to the first tab, focus ring appears but there’s no persistent visual cue distinguishing active vs focused state beyond color contrast of underline.  
  - Fix: Ensure `:focus-visible` outline remains visible even when `.active` class is applied (currently both styles may conflict visually).

#### UX Design

- **No programmatic grouping or labeling of tablist region** — Screen Reader Semantic — MINOR — WCAG 1.3.1 Info and Relationships  
  - Evidence: `src/components/TabPanel.jsx` line 18 — `<div className="tab-bar">` has no accessible name (no `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, or associated heading). A screen reader user navigating by landmarks will not understand this is a tab interface without exploring each button.  
  - Fix: Add `aria-label="Product Details Tabs"` to `.tab-bar` div, or reference the existing `<h2>` via `aria-labelledby`.

- **Tab order does not follow expected linear sequence after panel switch** — Keyboard Motor — MINOR — WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order  
  - Evidence: `src/components/TabPanel.jsx` lines 37–43 — When switching tabs, focus remains on the clicked tab button but no mechanism ensures subsequent Tab keypresses move into newly revealed panel content in a predictable order. Panels are rendered sequentially in DOM regardless of visibility state.  
  - Fix: After activating a new tab, optionally shift focus to the associated panel or ensure logical reading/focus flow within it.

#### Content Author

- **Tab labels lack descriptive context beyond generic terms** — Screen Reader Semantic — ENHANCEMENT (AAA) — WCAG 2.4.6 Headings and Labels  
  - Evidence: `src/components/TabPanel.jsx` lines 5–10 — Tab labels ("Overview", "Specifications", etc.) are acceptable but could be more descriptive for screen reader users scanning by headings/links (e.g., “Product Overview”, “Technical Specifications”). This is an aspirational improvement, not a failure.  
  - Fix: Consider enhancing tab button text with additional context where helpful without changing visual design.

---

### Open Questions Requiring Human Verification

None — all findings are code-level and verifiable from source.

---

### Recommended Next Step

**REVISE** — Four MAJOR findings require addressing before shipping, primarily around ARIA implementation for the WAI-ARIA APG tab pattern (roles, states, properties) and keyboard arrow navigation support. These block full accessibility compliance for screen reader and keyboard-only users.
